bull_thesis:
The bull case is that LUCIDITY works, and that a company with no product today owns an approved, first-in-class orphan drug by 2027. Amylyx is running a pivotal Phase 3 trial of avexitide in post-bariatric hypoglycemia, a condition in which people who have had gastric bypass surgery suffer dangerous crashes in blood sugar. There is no approved treatment. Avexitide is a GLP-1 receptor antagonist: it blocks the same hormone pathway the well-known weight-loss drugs activate, which is precisely the pathway that causes the condition. The mechanism is coherent rather than hopeful.

The evidence supporting a win is unusually good for a small-cap biotech. In the earlier Phase 2b study the 90mg once-daily dose produced a 64% reduction in the combined rate of moderate and severe low-blood-sugar events, with more than half of participants having no events at all during treatment. That is a large effect measured on the same endpoint the Phase 3 is testing. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration agreed the primary endpoint in advance and has granted the drug Breakthrough Therapy Designation, a status that speeds review for serious unmet needs, so the regulatory path is cleaner than usual for a first-in-class product. LUCIDITY finished enrolling all 78 participants on 24 March 2026, on the schedule management set in November 2025, and topline results are guided for the third quarter of 2026 - roughly one to two months away.

The setup is also fully funded. A September 2025 share sale raised about $191 million net, leaving $279.8 million in cash and short-term investments at 31 March 2026 and a stated runway into 2028. There is no financing condition, no dilution overhang before the data, and no going-concern question. Management has hit every checkpoint it set on this programme.

If the trial succeeds, Amylyx moves from a binary bet to a de-risked, approved-path orphan asset with roughly 160,000 addressable U.S. patients and no competitor. That profile supports a share price in the high twenties to low thirties on its own, and adds a genuine takeover angle: a first-in-class asset adjacent to the GLP-1 franchises is exactly what a large metabolic-disease company might buy. The most bullish street target, from Guggenheim, sits at $40. The conditions this case depends on are simple and few: the effect size must carry from a small Phase 2b into a small Phase 3, and the placebo group must not respond unexpectedly well.
bear_thesis:
The bear case has two parts, and only the second one is really about the science.

First, the trial can miss. LUCIDITY enrolled 78 participants and is powered for the large effect Phase 2b suggested, which means it has very little cushion if the true effect is merely good rather than dramatic, or if the variance runs higher than expected. The primary endpoint counts symptomatic low-blood-sugar events, and endpoints built on counting patient-experienced events are notoriously vulnerable to placebo response and to measurement noise. Phase 2b was itself small. A fair reading puts the probability of success at 55% to 65% - better than an average Phase 3, but a long way from a formality. This management team also has direct experience of the failure mode: its ALS drug Relyvrio missed both primary and secondary endpoints in the PHOENIX Phase 3 on 8 March 2024, after the company had publicly championed it, and was subsequently withdrawn from the market.

Second, and more damaging at today's price, there is nothing underneath the stock if the trial misses. Almost the entire $2.17 billion market value rests on this one readout. The backup pipeline cannot absorb a failure: AMX0114 in ALS has only completed the first cohort of a Phase 1 safety study, and AMX0035 in Wolfram syndrome has published Phase 2 data but no pivotal programme. Cash will be roughly $200 to $220 million at readout, about $1.80 to $2.00 per share, against a share price of $19.49. The company's own history says a failed binary does not clear at cash: after PHOENIX, Amylyx held about $5.38 per share of cash and the stock still fell to an all-time low of $1.58 on 17 June 2024, roughly 29% of the cash on its balance sheet. Goldman Sachs cut its target from $40 to $4 within days.

What would confirm the bear case: a topline release that reports the primary endpoint as 'nominally' or 'directionally' favourable rather than statistically significant, a stronger-than-expected placebo response, or any delay past September 2026 that is not explained by a routine database lock. On a miss, a decline of 80% to 87% from here is the reasonable expectation, not the tail.
sop_bull: Event-win value: about $30 per share. Avexitide is the only part that matters. Assume approval in 2027 into roughly 160,000 addressable U.S. patients with no competing therapy, orphan-style pricing, and peak sales approaching $1 billion. A de-risked, approved, first-in-class orphan asset typically clears 3 to 4 times peak sales, giving an enterprise value of $3.0 to $3.5 billion. Add net cash of roughly $210 million at readout and divide by 111.2 million shares: $28.90 to $33.40, call it $30. The residual pipeline (AMX0114 in ALS at first-cohort Phase 1, AMX0035 in Wolfram syndrome at Phase 2, AMX0318 preclinical) contributes perhaps $1 to $2 per share of option value inside that range and is not counted separately. A takeout at a premium is the upside beyond this, and is where the $40 street high comes from, but it is optionality rather than a base case.
sop_bear: Verified downside floor: about $3 per share - materially below the $4.00 the board's dossier carried. Cash and short-term investments were $279.8 million at 31 March 2026, burning $37 to $42 million a quarter, so roughly $200 to $220 million remains at readout - about $1.80 to $2.00 per share. consensus_delta:
There is no disagreement with the market left to harvest, and that is the finding.

This funnel exists to buy events the market has mispriced. Here the market has priced the event about right. At $19.49, against a $30 win and a $3 loss, the price implies roughly 61% probability of success. An honest reading of the science - a 64% effect in Phase 2b, an endpoint agreed with the regulator, Breakthrough Therapy Designation, set against a 78-patient trial and an event-counting endpoint vulnerable to placebo response - lands at 55% to 65%. The market's number sits inside our range. There is nothing to arbitrage.

The street is not looking the wrong way; it is looking directly at this. The stock has run from a 52-week low of $7.48 to $19.49, up about 160%, and closed 27 July within pennies of its 52-week high of $19.60 after a 5.9% single-day gain. Where we do disagree with the consensus is on the downside, and it is the more useful disagreement. The board's own dossier carried a $4.00 floor, and the street generally frames the failure case around cash. Both are too generous. After the PHOENIX failure in March 2024 Amylyx held about $5.38 per share of cash and the stock still fell to $1.58 by 17 June 2024 - roughly 29% of the cash on the balance sheet. A failed binary does not clear at cash, because the entire holder base owns it for the event and leaves at once. Our verified floor is $3.00. That correction alone turns a superficially attractive setup into a negative-edge one.

The one place a genuine information edge might still exist is the success case's ceiling. The market's $1.9 billion enterprise value implies an approved avexitide worth about $3.2 billion at 60% odds. The post-bariatric hypoglycemia market was estimated at about $470 million across the seven major markets in 2025. Justifying that value requires avexitide both to expand the category substantially and to hold it uncontested. If the street is wrong about anything here, it is more likely to be the size of the prize on a win than the odds of winning.
valley_of_death:
The next three to nine months are not a slow grind - they are a single morning.

There is no cash-burn hump to survive and no maturity wall to clear. The September 2025 share sale, which raised about $191 million net, deliberately funded the company through this event: cash and short-term investments stood at $279.8 million at 31 March 2026 against a burn of roughly $37 to $42 million a quarter, with stated runway into 2028. That is the setup working as intended - management removed the financing risk before the binary, so there is no dilution overhang and no going-concern question in the window. Credit where it is due.

The risk is concentrated instead in one release. The realistic sequence of harm runs: (1) a soft reaffirmation at the 6 August 2026 second-quarter results - if 'third quarter' becomes 'second half', the stock gives back a meaningful part of its run on the delay alone, because a stock priced at its high for an imminent event cannot absorb a slip; (2) the readout itself, where a miss costs 80% to 87% in a session, on the direct precedent of the 82.2% single-day fall on 8 March 2024; (3) on a win, a fast re-rate followed by the grind of an unscheduled regulatory filing, since management has given no submission date and a 2027 launch remains an aspiration.

The asymmetry of the harm is what matters. On a win the stock probably reaches $28 to $32 and then waits, which is a 45% to 65% gain. On a loss it goes to $3 and stays there for a year, as it did in 2024. A position taken here is not exposed to a valley it can walk through; it is exposed to a step it either clears or falls off.
positioning_washout:
There is no forced-selling pressure to buy into here - the opposite is true, and that is the core problem with entering at this price.

This funnel makes its money buying assets whose holders are being pushed out for reasons unrelated to value: index deletions, deal breaks, dividend cuts that expel income funds, forced liquidations. None of that is present. The shareholder base has been assembling for this event, not fleeing it. The stock is up about 160% from its 52-week low of $7.48, sits within pennies of its 52-week high, and rose 5.9% on 27 July alone. Volume and price action into a known binary describe accumulation by event-driven money, not capitulation. There is no washed-out base to lean on and no reluctant seller to take stock from.

The forced selling in this name lies on the other side of the event, and it points the wrong way for a buyer today. On a failure, the mechanical liquidation is severe and one-directional: every holder who owns the shares specifically for the readout has no reason to keep them the moment it resolves badly, small-cap biotech funds have hard mandates against holding a failed lead asset, and the passive index holders sell mechanically as the market value collapses out of their thresholds. That is precisely the dynamic that drove the stock to $1.58 in June 2024 while it still held about $5.38 per share of cash - a cash-rich company sold below its cash because the entire holder base wanted out at once and no natural buyer existed.

The constructive way to read this: the wash-out is the opportunity, and it has not happened yet. Either it never does, because the trial works and the stock re-rates, or it happens violently and creates a genuinely mispriced cash-rich shell. Neither of those is a reason to pay $19.49 today.
moderator_conclusion:
The catalyst is excellent. The price is not. That is the whole judgement.

Take the event on its own terms first, because it deserves it. Amylyx has a fully enrolled pivotal trial with 78 participants dosed as of 24 March 2026, a 16-week treatment period that puts the last patient out around mid-July, and topline data guided for the third quarter of 2026 - guidance set in November 2025 and reaffirmed twice since. The endpoint was agreed with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in advance and the drug carries Breakthrough Therapy Designation. The event is funded through a September 2025 raise, so there is no financing condition and no dilution before the print. Management has hit every checkpoint it set on this programme. This is a live, hard, imminent, binding catalyst, and it would be wrong to mark it down as soft or unverifiable. We do not.

But the funnel's test has three legs, not one, and this setup passes only the first. The second leg asks whether the live price sits well below the event-resolved target. It does not: $19.49 against a $30 win is +54%, and the stock has already tripled from $7.48 into the print to close within pennies of its 52-week high. The third leg asks for a verified downside floor that bounds the loss. There isn't one. The board's dossier carried $4.00; cash at readout will be about $1.80 to $2.00 per share; and the governing precedent is brutal and specific - after its last Phase 3 failure this same company, holding about $5.38 per share of cash, saw its stock fall 82.2% in a day and reach $1.58 by June 2024, roughly 29% of cash. Our verified floor is $3.00, and the fall to it is 85%.

Put the two together and the arithmetic decides. At 60% odds - the midpoint of a fair 55% to 65% read - the probability-weighted value is $19.20 against a $19.49 price. The market has already priced this binary correctly, and is asking a small premium on top. Risking 85% to make 54% at those odds is not underwriting a mispriced event; it is accepting the market's own price on a coin flip. This is not the compounder cap being applied to a special situation - we are applying the special-situation test exactly as written, and the setup fails two of its three legs on price, not on the quality of the catalyst.

Hence wait, rather than pass outright, and wait for something specific. Two entries would make this a position. The first is a pullback to roughly $12, which would imply about 33% probability of success against a $30-versus-$3 payoff - a genuine discount to fair odds and a setup worth sizing; a soft reaffirmation at the 6 August 2026 results, or a broad biotech risk-off move, could deliver it. The second, and the one this book's own 2026 evidence favours, is to buy after a positive readout at $28 to $32, with the binary removed, an approved-path orphan asset in hand, and a takeover angle attached. Post-event re-rates in this book have kept running; guessing before the event has not paid. The discipline here is to keep the name on the watchlist through the print rather than own the coin flip.
interrogator_dossier:
# Amylyx Pharmaceuticals (AMLX) — Forensic Dossier on the Event

*Event-driven special situation. The question is not whether Amylyx is a good business — it has no
revenue and no franchise. The question is whether the spread between today's price and the
event-resolved value is wide enough to pay for the risk of the event going the wrong way.*

**As of 28 July 2026. Share price $19.49 (close, 27 July 2026). Market value about $2.17 billion on
111.2 million shares.**

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC — what this company became

Amylyx is on its second life. Its first drug, Relyvrio, won an unusual U.S. approval for ALS (a fatal
nerve disease) in 2022 on thin evidence, then failed its confirmatory Phase 3 trial, PHOENIX, on
8 March 2024. The stock fell 82.2% in a single session. The company pulled the drug from the market
and cut about 70% of its staff.

What it did next is the reason it is on this board. In July 2024 Amylyx bought avexitide — a
Phase 3-ready drug from the wreckage of Eiger BioPharmaceuticals — and rebuilt itself around it.
Avexitide is a GLP-1 receptor antagonist: it blocks the same hormone pathway that the well-known
weight-loss drugs activate. It is aimed at post-bariatric hypoglycemia, a condition in which people
who have had gastric bypass surgery suffer dangerous crashes in blood sugar. There is no approved
treatment. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted the drug Breakthrough Therapy
Designation, a status that speeds up review for drugs addressing serious unmet needs.

The narrative arc is therefore genuinely constructive: a management team that blew up a franchise
went out and bought a better-validated asset in a cleaner indication, and has executed the plan on
schedule since. That is a real turn, and it deserves credit. It does not, however, tell us anything
about whether the price today is a good one.

## 2. THE EVENT — is the catalyst real, dated, and binding?

**The event:** topline results from LUCIDITY, the pivotal Phase 3 trial of avexitide.

**Real:** Yes. The trial is fully enrolled and running. Amylyx announced on 24 March 2026 that the
last of 78 participants had been randomized and dosed. It is a 16-week, multicentre, randomised,
double-blind, placebo-controlled study — the highest-quality design available. The primary outcome
is a reduction in the combined rate of moderate and severe low-blood-sugar events through week 16,
and Amylyx states this endpoint was agreed with the FDA in advance. An agreed endpoint materially
reduces the risk of the "we hit our target but the regulator disagrees it matters" failure mode.

**Dated:** Partly. The guidance is "third quarter of 2026" — a quarter, not a day. There is no
regulatory decision date to anchor it, because this is a company-run data readout, not an agency
action. The important credibility point is that this quarter-guidance has been stable: Amylyx told
investors in its third-quarter 2025 results that enrollment would finish in the first quarter of
2026 and topline data would arrive in the third quarter of 2026. Enrollment finished 24 March 2026 —
inside the promised window — and the third-quarter data guidance was reaffirmed on 24 March 2026 and
again in the first-quarter results on 7 May 2026. Management has hit every checkpoint it set on this
programme.

**Binding:** In the sense that matters, yes. Once a trial is fully enrolled with a fixed 16-week
treatment period, the data exist and will be read out; there is no counterparty who can walk away,
no financing condition, no regulatory step that can be extended indefinitely. Enrollment finished in
late March, so the last patient completes 16 weeks around mid-July 2026, with database lock and
unblinding to follow. A readout in August or September 2026 is arithmetically consistent. The window
is genuinely imminent — roughly one to two months from today.

**Verdict on the event itself: this is about as clean a pending, dated, binding catalyst as this
funnel ever sees.** The problem, as section 5 shows, is not the catalyst. It is the price.

## 3. SPONSOR CREDIBILITY — two very different track records

This is where the forensic work matters, because Amylyx's record splits cleanly in two.

| Dimension | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Hitting stated timelines | Guided Q1-2026 enrollment in Nov 2025; delivered 24 Mar 2026. Reaffirmed Q3-2026 topline twice. | **Reliable.** No slippage on this programme. |
| Funding ahead of the event | Raised about $191 million net in a September 2025 share sale. Held $279.8 million in cash and short-term investments at 31 March 2026. | **Reliable.** The event is fully funded; no financing contingency, no pre-readout dilution overhang. |
| Predicting Phase 3 outcomes | PHOENIX failed both primary and secondary endpoints in March 2024 after management had publicly championed the drug. | **Discredited.** |
| Reading regulatory tea leaves | Relyvrio was approved over an initially negative advisory committee, then withdrawn. | **Discredited.** |

The distinction is important and easy to blur. Management is credible on *process* — they will
deliver the data when they said they would, and they have the cash to do it. They have no
demonstrated ability to tell you what the data will *say*, and one very expensive counter-example.
Do not let the first kind of credibility be borrowed to support the second.

**Evidence for the drug working, independent of management:** avexitide's Phase 2b trial showed a
64% least-squares mean reduction in the combined rate of moderate and severe hypoglycemic events at
the 90mg once-daily dose, with more than half of participants having no events at all during
treatment. That is a large effect on the same endpoint the Phase 3 is measuring, and it is the
single strongest reason to think LUCIDITY works. The mechanism is also coherent — the condition is
caused by excessive GLP-1 signalling, and the drug blocks GLP-1. This is not a hopeful mechanism in
search of an effect.

**Evidence against:** 78 participants is a small trial. It is powered for the large effect Phase 2b
suggested, which means it has little cushion if the true effect is more modest or the variance is
higher than expected. Endpoints built on counting symptomatic events are notoriously vulnerable to
placebo response and to measurement noise, and Phase 2b was itself small. The honest read is that
this is a *better-than-average* Phase 3 — call it 55% to 65% likely to succeed — not a formality.

## 4. THE DOWNSIDE FLOOR — this is where the thesis breaks

The board's dossier carries a downside floor of $4.00. **I cannot verify that floor, and the
company's own history argues it is roughly twice too generous.**

Start with what actually backstops the price. At 31 March 2026 Amylyx held $279.8 million in cash
and short-term investments. Quarterly cash burn runs about $37–42 million (first-quarter 2026 net
loss was $41.3 million, on $27.6 million of research spend and $16.2 million of overhead). By the
time the data read out, cash should be roughly $200–220 million, or about **$1.80 to $2.00 per
share**. Above that sits the residual pipeline: AMX0114, an ALS candidate that has only completed
the first cohort of a Phase 1 safety study, and AMX0035 in Wolfram syndrome, which has Phase 2 data
published in May 2026 but no pivotal programme. Neither is worth much in a market that has just
watched the lead asset fail.

Now the falsification test. After PHOENIX failed in March 2024, Amylyx held $371.4 million in cash
against roughly 69 million shares — about **$5.38 per share of cash**. The stock did not find a floor
at cash. It fell to an all-time low of **$1.58 on 17 June 2024**, roughly 29% of the cash on the
balance sheet, and stayed depressed for months. Goldman Sachs cut its price target from $40 to $4
within days of the failure.

That is not a modelled scenario. It is what happened, to this company, to this shareholder base,
after this kind of event. A failed binary in small-cap biotech does not clear at cash, because the
holders who own it for the event all leave at once and the buyers who would pay for cash demand a
large discount against the risk that management spends it.

**My verified floor is therefore $3.00, not $4.00** — cash of roughly $2.00 per share plus a modest
allowance for a pipeline that is genuinely deeper than the post-PHOENIX shell was, tempered by the
$1.58 precedent. From $19.49, that is a fall of about 85%. In plain terms: **there is no floor here
worth the name.** This is a cliff with a small ledge near the bottom.

## 5. THE SPREAD — has it already closed?

This is the decisive number, and it is unflattering.

The stock has run from a 52-week low of $7.48 to $19.49 — up about 160% — and closed 27 July within
pennies of its 52-week high of $19.60, rising 5.9% on that single day. The market has not overlooked
this catalyst; it has been front-running it for months. Analyst targets have been chasing the price
up rather than leading it: H.C. Wainwright to $20, Mizuho to $24 on 20 July 2026, Guggenheim to $40
with a "best idea" tag ahead of the readout. The consensus target of roughly $23 to $25 sits barely
above the live price.

Work out what the price already assumes. With a success case around $30 and a verified failure case
around $3, a $19.49 price implies the market is already assigning about **61%** probability to
success. That is very close to my own honest estimate of 55–65%. **The market is pricing this binary
approximately correctly.** There is no meaningful disagreement left to arbitrage.

Sense-check the success case so the upside is not being understated. Enterprise value — market value
less net cash — is about $1.9 billion today. At 60% odds that implies the market already values an
approved avexitide at roughly $3.2 billion. Against a post-bariatric hypoglycemia market estimated
at about $470 million across the seven major markets in 2025, avexitide would have to both expand
that market substantially and hold it alone to justify peak sales near $1 billion. A $3.2 billion
value on $1 billion of eventual peak sales is a full, though not absurd, price for a de-risked
orphan asset. The success case simply does not have much headroom above $30 unless a larger company
buys the whole thing at a premium — a real possibility for a first-in-class asset in a GLP-1-adjacent
field, but that is optionality, not the base case.

## 6. RED FLAGS AND GREEN FLAGS

**Concerning**
- The stock sits at its 52-week high going into a coin-flip-plus event. Everyone who wants to own
  the catalyst already does. There is no forced-selling pressure to buy into and no washed-out base.
- The downside floor in the board's dossier ($4.00) is unsupported. The company's own 2024 low of
  $1.58 — struck while holding $5.38 per share in cash — is the governing precedent.
- Only 78 participants. A trial powered for a large effect has little room for a merely good one.
- This management team has already lost a Phase 3 and had to withdraw an approved drug.
- Nearly the entire enterprise value rests on one asset with one readout. The backup pipeline cannot
  absorb a failure; AMX0114 has only first-cohort Phase 1 safety data.

**Encouraging**
- The event is funded. The September 2025 raise removed the financing risk, so there is no dilution
  overhang and no going-concern question before the data.
- Management has hit every milestone on this programme and reaffirmed the quarter twice.
- The endpoint was agreed with the FDA in advance, and the drug holds Breakthrough Therapy
  Designation — the regulatory path is unusually clean for a first-in-class product.
- The Phase 2b effect size was large and the mechanism is coherent, not speculative.
- No approved competitor exists in the indication.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The Expanded Access Program launched in May 2026, offering avexitide to up to 250 adults outside the
trial, is quietly informative. Companies rarely stand up a programme of that size, at their own cost,
for a drug they expect to fail — it is a genuine, if soft, tell about how management reads the
blinded safety picture. It is not evidence about efficacy, which is what LUCIDITY tests.

The second signal is what management is *not* saying: there is still no specific date for the
regulatory filing, only "early preparations underway." That is appropriate caution, but it means
approval and launch remain a 2027 aspiration rather than a scheduled step.

## 8. VERDICT FOR THE DIRECTOR

The single thing to weigh before sizing this: **the catalyst is excellent and the price is not.**

Everything this funnel looks for in an event-driven position is present except the one thing that
actually generates the return — a spread. The event is real, imminent, binding, funded, and run by a
team that has kept every date it set. But the stock has already tripled into it and now sits at its
high, the market's implied odds match a fair reading of the science, and the downside is not a floor
but an 85% fall to a level this company has visited before under exactly these circumstances.

Risking 85% to make 50%, at roughly 60/40 odds, is a bet with no edge and a fat left tail. Buying it

# AMLX - Amylyx Pharmaceuticals - Interrogator Dossier (Event-Driven Special Situation)

**Frame:** This is NOT a quality/compounding judgment. AMLX is a clinical-stage biotech with no approved product and negative earnings - cheap-and-bad on every franchise metric BY DESIGN. The thesis is the SPREAD between the live price (~$15.67, Jun 18 close; $15.88 pre-mkt Jun 22) and the event-resolved value of a HARD-DATED, data-driven binary: the pivotal Phase 3 LUCIDITY topline readout for avexitide in post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), guided to Q3 2026 (board hard date 2026-09-30, ~105d). The interrogation is of the EVENT, not the moat.

## 1. IS THE CATALYST REAL, DATED, AND BINDING?
REAL - yes. LUCIDITY is a registrational, FDA-agreed pivotal Phase 3 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled), 78 participants, 3:2 avexitide 90 mg QD vs placebo, 16-week double-blind period, 21 U.S. sites, in adults with PBH following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Primary endpoint: reduction in composite Level 2 + Level 3 hypoglycemic events at Week 16. Avexitide carries FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation - there is NO FDA-approved therapy for PBH (~160,000 U.S. patients, 8,000-12,000 new RYGB cases/yr).
DATED - yes, and tightening. Topline repeatedly guided to Q3 2026 ('on track,' reaffirmed Q1 2026 results, May 2026). Enrollment completed March 2026 - the clock to a 16-week-primary readout is now mechanical, not enrollment-dependent. Hard board date 2026-09-30 sits at the back edge of the guided Q3 window.
BINDING - yes. A clean clinical binary (data event), not a deal contingent on a counterparty, financing, or regulator's discretion. No second-request, no CVR, no financing contingency.

## 2. SPONSOR / MANAGEMENT CREDIBILITY
Mixed but improving, materially de-risked by design. Bear anchor: prior drug AMX0035 (Relyvrio) FAILED its confirmatory PHOENIX Phase 3 in ALS (2024) and was withdrawn - a real scar. BUT avexitide is structurally stronger: replicated signal across FIVE prior PBH trials (Phase 2b: 64% LS-mean reduction at 90 mg QD - the exact dose/endpoint now in LUCIDITY; Phase 2 PREVENT: 50%/75% fewer rescues); overpowered design (>95% power per H.C. Wainwright); Stifel 75% PoS, HCW ~60% approval prob; board win_prob 0.62. Management pivoted post-Relyvrio, raised cash, acquired a de-risked Phase-3-ready BTD asset.

## 3. VERIFIED DOWNSIDE FLOOR
Hard cash floor ~$2.53/share: $279.8M cash/ST-investments (Mar 31 2026) / ~110.6M wtd-avg shares; runway into 2028; no going-concern, no maturity wall, no covenant, no forced pre-event ATM. Realistic post-failure clearing ~$4.00 (board floor) vs 52-wk low $4.80: a PBH miss does not zero AMLX - it retains net cash, residual avexitide optionality, and a live second program AMX0114 (antisense, ALS), Phase 1 LUMINA, ENCALS biomarker data June 2026. The $4 floor = cash + haircut pipeline stub; the loss is bounded.

## 4. RED FLAGS
Single-binary, single-asset event; re-rate from $4.80 to $18.61 already priced meaningful success, so ~$15.67 is NOT a washed-out entry. Management's PHOENIX/Relyvrio failure; small n=78. Cash-per-share ($2.53) is below the $4 floor - the floor leans on pipeline-option value the market could refuse to pay on a sentiment-crushing miss. Post-success dilutive raise likely (known overhang).

## 5. GREEN FLAGS
Enrollment DONE (Mar 2026) -> mechanical date. Same dose/endpoint/population that worked across 5 trials; overpowered (>95%). BTD + zero-competition orphan -> fast premium launch (HCW $815M 2033 sales; launch 2027). Defined-risk: near-cash floor, no going-concern, clean binary. Street targets $21-$34 bracket the $28 board target.

## CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT
A genuine PENDING_HARD defined-risk special situation: binding, fully-enrolled, overpowered pivotal Phase 3 binary, Q3 2026 mechanical readout, corroborated $28 win target (street $21-$34), credible near-cash ~$4 floor. The director must weigh that the re-rate off the $4.80 low has ALREADY occurred - at $15.67 the asymmetry is GOOD but not pristine (+79% to $28 vs -74% to $4), carried by a ~62-75% PoS that tilts EV positive (+29%). Moat/secular N/A.
